pr.title: Plan reading committed configuration from the default branch, with overrides
pr.head: 8e46a04d71039cc1cb59f56c30776073a180057f

summary: Projector reads layered .projector.toml settings that control reviews, output paths, and relay destinations. This plan makes tracked settings come from the reviewed default branch rather than a contributor's working copy.

Priority overrides let outer configuration win deliberately. Destination approval, path containment, cached blob reads, and background default-branch refresh complete the proposed policy. The plan is ready/now; this pull request adds no implementation.

cards.title: Two decisions need correction
cards.html:
• The specified fetch still updates the user's remote-tracking ref unless configured mappings are disabled.
  • The overview permits an external user-level project path while the runtime rule forbids it.

groups.title: Make reviewed policy govern every checkout
groups.kicker: Default-branch sources, explicit overrides, and local consent
intro: Tracked configuration is read from the default-branch commit shared by a repository's worktrees. Untracked and user configuration stays on disk. Overrides use priorities from 1 to 99, with farther files winning ties.

Destination values from tracked files require terminal approval. The daemon refreshes its private default-branch ref on full passes, while cached reads avoid processes on warm loads. The per-checkout local-file and superproject questions are explicitly deferred.

files.note: Defines the configuration source, override precedence, destination approval, path rules, refresh command, and acceptance cases.

checks.text: The priority and equal-priority distance rules agree across the runtime flow, rationale, decision record, and acceptance cases.
A temporary clone shows this fetch advances the configured origin tracking ref as well as Projector's ref. Add --refmap= to honor the no-origin-mutation contract.
The overview exempts a user-level projects.dir from containment, but this rule refuses it from every file. Choose one behavior and include its user-file acceptance case.
project check and project show confirm valid ready/now metadata. The two remaining scope questions are deliberately deferred.
